# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Taylor Kimura**
[Street address]
[City], KS [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-07-31
**Member:** Taylor Kimura
**Member ID:** W354999576
**Reference number:** POC-37F3AA304D-16940
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing Cigna's denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), issued on 2026-07-31 under reference number POC-37F3AA304D-16940. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records in the prior authorization packet speak to each of the categories of criteria in the plan's own policy. Below I set those criteria side by side with what my records actually say. Where my records do not squarely answer a point, I say so plainly rather than overstate it, and I ask Cigna to tell me exactly what additional document it needs.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Imaging.** The policy states:

> "Imaging shows BOTH of the following findings:"

and

> "femoroacetabular impingement confirmed on x-ray, MRI, or CT with ANY of the following findings:"

with the listed findings including:

> "presence of Tönnis Grade 0-1 osteoarthritis"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-06-24 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, with joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0. Femoroacetabular impingement is therefore confirmed on MRI, and the Tönnis grade documented in my imaging report falls within the Grade 0-1 range the policy names. The policy also lists other imaging findings, including "decrease of femoral head-neck offset" and "acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign)"; the policy requires only ANY of those findings, and my report documents the Tönnis grade.

**2. Physical exam.** The policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings:"

and names:

> "positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation)"

and

> "limited passive hip internal rotation"

My exam record documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I want to be accurate with you: the summary I have does not spell out the provocative maneuver by name or record passive internal rotation as a separate measurement. If that specific wording is what the reviewer was looking for, that is a documentation detail, not a clinical gap, and Dr. Okafor's office can supply the full exam note. I am asking Cigna to request it rather than deny the surgery over it.

**3. Non-surgical management.** The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

and includes:

> "an image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within two (2) weeks after the injection)"

I completed supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification from 2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15 — 16 weeks, 24 visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief. I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21, which gave me four weeks of partial relief. That is a positive response — my pain was reduced — and the relief did not last. My records as summarized do not state whether that injection was image-guided and intra-articular; that detail is in [the procedure note for the 2026-03-21 injection, available from the administering provider]. Again, I ask that Cigna request this record.

**4. Symptoms.** The policy states:

> "Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and that significantly limits activities"

This describes my situation precisely. I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain that rest does not relieve. I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I cannot run or squat.

## A note about the criteria I was given

Several of the policy provisions quoted above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not able to address requirements I have not seen. Because this denial was issued for incomplete documentation, I am asking Cigna to identify, in writing, the specific criteria from Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 that it applied to my request and the specific document or finding it found missing. With that, my surgeon and I can respond directly instead of guessing.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial of 2026-07-31 and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, as requested by Dr. Okafor. In the alternative, I ask that Cigna tell me exactly which records it needs and hold my appeal open so those records can be submitted. I would also like a copy of the complete criteria applied to my case and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-01-27, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I can also be reached through Cigna Customer Service at 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I am happy to provide anything further that would help.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Kimura**
Member ID: W354999576
Date of birth: [DOB]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]

**Enclosures:** [MRI arthrogram report, 2026-06-24] · [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15] · [Office/exam notes, Dr. Okafor, MD] · [Injection procedure note, 2026-03-21] · [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-07-31]
